emerging_technology: Multimodal generative AI for short-form social video creation and content governance
intended_application: Create draft 15-60 second TikTok and Instagram marketing videos from approved product assets, with human review before publication and provenance/disclosure controls for AI-generated media
organization: Harbor Glow, a hypothetical 25-person direct-to-consumer beauty company selling in the United States
industry_sector: Small consumer beauty brand and digital advertising
business_need: Increase short-video output without adding agency cost or full-time production staff
users_stakeholders: Founder, two-person marketing team, freelance creators, customers, social platforms, product counsel on retainer, performers and rights holders
adoption_posture: Aggressive early adopter seeking immediate production gains
capabilities_constraints: Founder sponsorship and fast decisions; no dedicated legal, privacy, information-security or AI-governance staff; marketing assets stored across shared drives; freelancers use personal accounts; no formal content approval workflow; no training budget; one marketer would operate and approve outputs; monthly tool budget capped at USD 1,500
risk_consequence_context: Public-facing beauty claims, realistic synthetic people, consent and likeness, intellectual-property and platform-labeling risks. Rapid publication and limited review capacity make errors likely to reach customers before detection
management_question: Should management begin using the technology for public short-video campaigns next month, and what must change first?
time_horizon: Public launch proposed within 30 days; six-month operating horizon
additional_context: The same employee would generate, review and publish content. Vendor terms, training-data assurances, incident response, provenance retention and approval evidence have not been evaluated.
